briefing:
# Analyst investigation exercise

You are a junior analyst at a fictional financial institution. At 11:12 UTC on 15 April 2026, six alerts are waiting for review. Two new accounts have each received a large project payment and submitted two outgoing orders. Your task is to investigate the records and explain what action the available evidence supports.

All people, businesses, accounts, watchlist entries, documents, and amounts are invented for this exercise. SCU means fictional scenario currency units. The supplied course policy governs this exercise.

## Records to examine

- [Customer profiles](customers.json) describe declared activity.
- [Accounts](accounts.csv) identify the holders and opening balances.
- [Transactions](transactions.csv) contain 126 transfers, including four pending orders.
- [Alerts](alerts.csv) give the review queue.
- [Evidence index](evidence-index.csv) links the twelve records available at the start.
- [Request catalog](request-catalog.csv) lists further checks and their simulated service times.
- [Course policy](course-policy.md) explains verification, provisional controls, and documentation.

The ledger is a snapshot. A pending order has not reduced the account balance. A blank execution timestamp is intentional. Previous-institution statement excerpts are separate evidence and are not additional rows in this bank’s ledger.

## Investigation tasks

1. Prioritise the alerts and explain your order of review.
2. Compare each customer’s declared activity with the account and payment records.
3. Identify which statements are claims, which have independent support, and which facts are still missing.
4. Ask the instructor for checks using a customer ID and a request ID. The instructor supplies responses after their service time and prerequisites are satisfied.
5. Record the evidence IDs you relied on, your decision, any provisional control, and the simulated time at which you acted.
6. Explain when you would revisit your decision and what additional evidence could change it.

## Case note template

Alert and customer:

Review time:

Payment status at decision time:

Observed activity and expected activity:

Evidence IDs examined:

Unverified claims and remaining gaps:

Recommended action and reason:

Hold start or release time, if applicable:

Next review or escalation:

No video file is included. The KYC records contain a transcript and authored observations for a text-based exercise.
policy:
# Fictional course investigation policy

This policy applies only to the TwinAML classroom exercise. Its alert thresholds and verification rules are authored assumptions, not a statement of law or a bank’s actual procedures.

## Identity verification

Quality observations such as lighting changes or irregular blink timing trigger review. They do not prove manipulation. An inconclusive capture is different from a failed challenge.

Two recorded failed challenges stop onboarding under this policy. Any exception must retain the original results and its reason, and must be reviewed. A successful repeat verification can resolve an inconclusive first capture when its log is independently checked.

## Payment alert

The NEW_ACCOUNT_CREDIT_AND_FANOUT alert is generated when an account opened within a day receives at least 300000 SCU and submits outgoing orders totalling at least 90 percent of that receipt within 30 minutes. This is an exercise alert rule; it is not a threshold for proving or reporting a crime.

Review the expected activity, payer, authority, recipients, documents, and payment status. Large amounts, rapid splits, a virtual-asset business category, or a potential name match each need context.

## Evidence and screening

Customer emails and submitted invoices are claims until checked. Use verified contact routes for independent confirmation. Resolve possible name matches using multiple identifiers. Resolving one match does not resolve unrelated concerns. These screening records use a wholly fictional watchlist.

## Provisional controls

An analyst may request an immediate provisional outbound hold during this exercise when a material identity or funds concern is unresolved. Record the concern, the time, and the next check. Apply the control proportionately and reconsider it when evidence arrives.

An effective hold prevents a pending order from executing at its due time. It does not undo a completed transfer. A drafted report or an escalation does not automatically place a hold.

When a temporary hold is released, an overdue order may execute immediately after an eligibility check. Check funds and order status again. At equal timestamps, an accepted hold is applied before an order’s due check. These timing conventions are classroom assumptions.

## Closure and escalation

Escalate a concern when material contradictions remain, explaining the evidence and uncertainty. Close a resolved alert with a reasoned note identifying the evidence that answers the concern. The exercise involves an internal draft and recommendation; it does not submit a report to any authority.

You are assessed on the information available when you decided. You are not expected to prove hidden scenario facts. A provisional review can be justified even when later checks resolve the alert.

evidence.title: Account application
evidence.body:
# Account application

Synthetic training record.

Record: EV-001

Customer: SYN-001

Source: Customer submission

Application received: 15 April 2026, 10:00 UTC.

Mira Solen describes their work as event installation and technical support. The declared monthly income is 28000 SCU. Expected credits are salary and expense reimbursement, usually from the employer or known project clients, with a largest expected single credit of 40000 SCU.

The applicant says that occasional purchasing work is part of the job. The application does not name a purchasing client, provide an agency agreement, or list virtual-asset settlement as an expected activity.

The applicant requests a current account for work payments. Contact correspondence is through the customer portal; no real telephone number, address, identity document, or signature is supplied in this exercise.

evidence.title: Video verification intake summary
evidence.body:
# Video verification intake summary

Synthetic training record.

Record: EV-002

Customer: SYN-001

Source: Onboarding operations

Video intake recorded two quality observations: irregular blink intervals and inconsistent face lighting. The reviewer notes that these observations require further checking and do not establish impersonation.

The account was opened at 10:45 UTC following an onboarding exception. This summary does not include the full challenge log or the exception approval narrative. They can be requested from the verification team.

The initial video transcript reads:

> Reviewer: Please state why you need the account.
> Applicant: I work on events. I will receive work payments and pay for equipment.
> Reviewer: Will payments come from your employer?
> Applicant: Usually. Sometimes another person settles the project.

No video file is attached to this text-only training export.

evidence.title: Payment alert detail
evidence.body:
# Payment alert detail

Synthetic training record.

Record: EV-003

Customer: SYN-001

Source: Training bank monitoring

At 11:10 UTC, SYN-A001 received 480000 SCU from Corven Services, account SYN-X01, with reference PROJECT 0415. The customer then submitted two outgoing orders: 230000 SCU to Neris Settlement Desk at 11:30 UTC and 240000 SCU to Valen Settlement Desk at 11:35 UTC.

Both outgoing orders remain pending at the exercise snapshot, 11:12 UTC. They represent 470000 / 480000, or approximately 97.9 percent, of the incoming amount. Their recipient trading activities have not yet been verified.

The credit is larger than the maximum single credit declared in the application. The alert combines this activity with the unresolved onboarding quality observations. It does not classify a crime or confirm the identity of the applicant.

Customer explanations, payment purpose, payer identity, and supporting documents need to be reconciled.

evidence.title: Customer portal message
evidence.body:
# Customer portal message

Synthetic training record.

Record: EV-004

Customer: SYN-001

Source: Customer correspondence

Received at 11:11 UTC.

> The payment is for an event project. The client uses a collection company, so the sender name will be different. I am arranging two supplier payments and keeping 10000 as my fee. The event starts soon. Please allow both transfers today; I can send an invoice if needed.

The message does not name the underlying client or attach a collection-authority document. Its statements are customer claims awaiting corroboration.

evidence.title: Verification team response
evidence.body:
# Verification team response

Synthetic training record.

Record: EV-005

Customer: SYN-001

Source: Independent synthetic verification team

The full challenge log records a failed challenge at 10:05 UTC and a second failed challenge at 10:25 UTC. Both attempts contain the same two quality observations. The log marks the requested head movement as not completed in the expected sequence.

An exception was approved at 10:45 UTC with the note: “Customer has an urgent project payment; open the account while further identity evidence is gathered.” No successful verification result is attached to that exception.

Under the supplied classroom policy, two recorded failures require a stop at onboarding; an exception must be documented and reviewed. This response establishes the recorded failures and exception. It does not provide a validated forensic conclusion about video authenticity.

evidence.title: Project invoice supplied by customer
evidence.body:
# Project invoice supplied by customer

Synthetic training record.

Record: EV-006

Customer: SYN-001

Source: Customer submission

Invoice reference: INV-0415. Supplier or agent: Mira Solen. Billed to: Tavren Event Works, synthetic business reference SYN-B007. Project: stage equipment coordination.

| Component | SCU |
| --- | ---: |
| Equipment payment A | 230000 |
| Equipment payment B | 240000 |
| Coordination fee | 10000 |
| Total | 480000 |

The invoice lists Neris Settlement Desk and Valen Settlement Desk as payment recipients. It names Tavren Event Works as the client, whereas the bank credit names Corven Services as the payer. There is no separate collection authority, purchase order, delivery record, or recipient invoice attached.

The invoice is a customer-supplied document. Its authenticity and commercial purpose have not been established by its arithmetic.

evidence.title: Payer and invoice verification response
evidence.source: Independent synthetic registry and payer liaison
evidence.body:
# Payer and invoice verification response

Synthetic training record.

Record: EV-007

Customer: SYN-001

Source: Independent synthetic registry and payer liaison

The registry entry for SYN-B007 names Tavren Event Works. Its verified contact route was used for this response. The representative says that invoice INV-0415 is absent from the issued purchase-order records and that no collection authority for Corven Services is recorded.

The payment-message check confirms that Corven Services is the account holder of SYN-X01. A request to Corven Services has not produced a contract or an explanation linking the payment to the customer’s stated event work.

The response contradicts the claimed client relationship and leaves the source and purpose of the credit unresolved. It does not establish the origin of every unit of the funds or prove that a named person committed an offence.

evidence.title: Name screening review
evidence.body:
# Name screening review

Synthetic training record.

Record: EV-008

Customer: SYN-001

Source: Synthetic screening desk

A fictional training watchlist returned a possible politically exposed person name match for Mira Solen. The listed person was born on 2 November 1961; the submitted customer profile gives 18 February 1994. The listed occupation and region also differ.

The screening desk records the match as a different-person match on the supplied identifiers. No matching sanctions entry is returned by this fictional dataset.

Resolving this name match answers the screening question. It does not resolve the separate identity-verification, source-of-funds, or payment-purpose concerns.

evidence.title: Recipient business checks
evidence.body:
# Recipient business checks

Synthetic training record.

Record: EV-009

Customer: SYN-001

Source: Independent synthetic recipient registry

SYN-X02 belongs to Neris Settlement Desk and SYN-X03 to Valen Settlement Desk. Their registry entries describe virtual-asset settlement services. No equipment-sale or equipment-rental trading activity is listed in these synthetic entries.

Neither recipient has supplied an equipment invoice for PROJECT 0415. The supplied customer invoice describes them as equipment recipients but provides no supporting relationship document.

A virtual-asset business category alone does not establish wrongdoing. The inconsistency with the claimed equipment purpose is the finding that requires investigation.

evidence.title: Response to account history request
evidence.body:
# Response to account history request

Synthetic training record.

Record: EV-010

Customer: SYN-001

Source: Customer correspondence

> I do not have the old account statement available. An assistant arranged this payment and can send more papers later. I do not want to repeat the video call today. Please use the invoice already sent and release the supplier payments.

No prior statement, named assistant authority, or independent source-of-funds record accompanies the response. The new account has no transactions before today in the supplied bank ledger. A reluctance to provide a document is a gap to record, rather than proof of a crime.

evidence.title: Verification team response
evidence.body:
# Verification team response

Synthetic training record.

Record: EV-015

Customer: SYN-002

Source: Independent synthetic verification team

The first capture at 10:05 UTC was marked inconclusive because of video frame loss and changing light. It was not recorded as a failed challenge. The customer completed a new verification at 10:25 UTC using a stable connection.

The repeat record marks the requested challenge sequence as completed and the identity review as passed. The account was opened at 10:50 UTC after that result; no exception approval was used.

The initial blink and lighting observations remain in the history. They are explained in the technical log as capture-quality observations in this authored exercise. This is a simulated review result, not a measurement from a real deepfake detector.

evidence.title: Project contract and supplier invoices
evidence.body:
# Project contract and supplier invoices

Synthetic training record.

Record: EV-016

Customer: SYN-002

Source: Customer submission

Contract reference: PC-0415. Client: Asterline Productions, SYN-B104. Coordinator: Nika Vale. Project: one installation and equipment rental package.

| Component | Recipient account | SCU |
| --- | --- | ---: |
| Equipment purchase, invoice NE-0415 | SYN-X05 | 230000 |
| Equipment rental, invoice VS-0415 | SYN-X06 | 240000 |
| Coordination fee | Retained by coordinator | 10000 |
| Total budget | | 480000 |

The contract authorises the coordinator to receive the project budget and pay the two named suppliers. Supplier invoices quote PROJECT 0415, the same recipient account numbers, and delivery or rental dates of 15 April 2026.

These copies were supplied by the customer. Independent confirmation of the payer, authority, and recipient details remains a separate check.

evidence.title: Payer and contract verification response
evidence.source: Independent synthetic registry and payer liaison
evidence.body:
# Payer and contract verification response

Synthetic training record.

Record: EV-017

Customer: SYN-002

Source: Independent synthetic registry and payer liaison

The verified registry contact for Asterline Productions, SYN-B104, confirms contract PC-0415, coordinator Nika Vale, the 480000 SCU budget, and the authority to pay the two named suppliers.

The confirmation was obtained through the registry contact route rather than a contact provided solely in the customer email. The payment-message check confirms that SYN-X04 belongs to Asterline Productions and that PROJECT 0415 is the payment reference.

The confirmed components are 230000 SCU for the equipment supplier, 240000 SCU for the rental supplier, and 10000 SCU retained as the coordinator’s fee. The confirmed amounts and parties reconcile to the bank records.

Customer: SYN-002

Source: Synthetic screening desk

A fictional training watchlist returned a possible politically exposed person name match for Nika Vale. The listed person was born on 7 July 1959; the submitted customer profile gives 3 September 1991. The listed occupation and region also differ.

The screening desk records the match as a different-person match on the supplied identifiers. No matching sanctions entry is returned by this fictional dataset.

The result resolves this name match. It does not by itself validate the project payment or the customer’s identity verification.

evidence.title: Recipient business checks
evidence.body:
# Recipient business checks

Synthetic training record.

Record: EV-019

Customer: SYN-002

Source: Independent synthetic recipient registry

SYN-X05 belongs to Neris Equipment Supply, whose recorded trading activity is event equipment sales. SYN-X06 belongs to Valen Stage Rentals, whose recorded trading activity is equipment rental.

The verified supplier contact routes confirm invoices NE-0415 and VS-0415, recipient accounts SYN-X05 and SYN-X06, the project reference, and the amounts of 230000 and 240000 SCU respectively.

These confirmations support the commercial purpose stated in the contract. Similar fragments in a business name are not a substitute for checking the account holder and verified trading activity.

# Expense reimbursement file

Synthetic training record.

Record: EV-021

Customer: SYN-003

Source: Existing bank file

An expense claim for project REV0412 records an 8200 SCU payment from Tarin Voss on 12 April and employer reimbursement on 14 April. The linked bank rows are TX-B3-028 and TX-B3-030. Both use the same reference and amount, with opposite directions.

# Translation invoice file

Synthetic training record.

Record: EV-022

Customer: SYN-004

Source: Existing bank file

Invoice TR-042 totals 8000 SCU and permits two instalments of 4000 SCU. Tavren Publishing paid instalments on 12 April and 14 April. The linked bank rows are TX-B4-028 and TX-B4-030.

The client account in both rows is the usual account in this supplied history. The repeated reference alone does not tell you whether the payment is duplicated; reconcile the two credits with the invoice total.

evidence.title: Club reserve transfer file
evidence.body:
# Club reserve transfer file

Synthetic training record.

Record: EV-023

Customer: SYN-005

Source: Existing bank file

Club minutes authorise a 12000 SCU transfer to SYN-X15, the club reserve account, on 14 April. The supplied ownership record identifies SYN-X15 as the club’s reserve account. The linked row is TX-B5-030.

This is the first reserve transfer in the supplied month of history. Check the ownership record and authorisation before deciding how to handle the unfamiliar-payee alert.

evidence.title: Repair order refund file
evidence.body:
# Repair order refund file

Synthetic training record.

Record: EV-024

Customer: SYN-006

Source: Existing bank file

Repair order RP-0412 records a 3200 SCU receipt on 12 April and a full refund on 14 April after the customer declined replacement parts. The linked rows are TX-B6-028 and TX-B6-030. The receipt and refund use the same settlement pool and reference.

The refund does not create a second sale. Reconcile the amounts and directions and record the remaining net receipt for this order.
